text: 想让 DSH 在提交消息前自动加上固定说明。
我需要按关键词替换用户提示里的某些文字。
怎样给每条请求套上统一的模板？
能不能只在会话第一轮应用提示规则？
希望通过对话新增或禁用持久化的提示规则。
如何把一段补充文字追加到用户消息末尾？
I want to wrap each submitted prompt in a reusable template.
Can I replace matching terms in my DSH messages automatically?
提示词前置与追加：插件按规则把文字插入消息的首个或末个文本块，并可配置分隔符。规则在 agent/pre-step 阶段匹配后生效。
整体替换或字面替换：规则可替换消息文本，或在各文本块中替换匹配字面串，并保留非文本内容。通过模式和匹配条件触发。
模板包装：使用唯一的 {{prompt}} 标记将原消息包在指定前后文本中，保持图像等非文本块顺序。由匹配的 template 规则触发。
对话管理规则：prompt_rewrite_rules 工具可列出、新增、启用、停用或删除规则；持久化变更会请求人工批准。
dsh-prompt-rewrite 是 DSH 提示词改写插件，在 agent/pre-step 阶段处理新的人类消息。它按优先级应用持久规则，支持前置、追加、整体替换、字面匹配替换和模板包装。规则保存于 DSH 设置，可通过会话工具管理，并按文本条件或轮次筛选。适合统一提示格式或替换术语，无需 API 密钥和外部服务。

dsh-prompt-rewrite applies persistent rules to new DSH messages. It supports prefixes, suffixes, replacement, and template wrapping, ordered by priority. A conversation tool manages saved rules. Use it to standardize prompts without an API key or external service.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · dsh-prompt-rewrite：An independent [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle for persistent, live prompt-rewrite rules. It is inference-provider agnostic and can be installed with the local `dsh-ds4` bundle or with any other model backend.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · dsh-prompt-rewrite：The plugin rewrites newly submitted human messages on root agents through the cooperative `agent/pre-step` waterfall. It waits for downstream plugins, preserves a downstream rejection, and retains message ids, sources, images, and other non-text blocks. Plugin context, tool results, and in-process subagent prompts are never rewritten.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Install from GitHub：From a DeepSeek Harness checkout, add the GitHub bundle to every DSH profile that should use it:

```sh
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add github:c4pt0r/dsh-prompt-rewrite
pnpm dsh plugin --profile headless add github:c4pt0r/dsh-prompt-rewrite
```

Profiles are independent. Installing the Web profile does not implicitly enable the plugin in headless or TUI profiles.

For local development, clone this repository, install its locked dependencies, and pass its path to the same command:

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Install from GitHub：```sh
git clone https://github.com/c4pt0r/dsh-prompt-rewrite.git
cd dsh-prompt-rewrite
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm test

Verify composition with:

```sh
pnpm dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

The result should contain a `dsh-prompt-rewrite` row whose plugin name is `dsh-prompt-rewrite/prompt-rewrite`.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：The runtime plugin and conversation tool are self-contained in this repository. The Web card additionally requires a Harness build that includes the `dsh-prompt-rewrite` settings allowlist and card. On an older unmodified Harness, the plugin still rewrites prompts and exposes its tool, but no Web card appears.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：Open **Settings → Plugins → Plugin configuration → Prompt rewrite rules**. The rule card supports adding, editing, enabling/disabling, reordering by priority, and deleting rules. Saving writes the shared `dsh-prompt-rewrite.rules` section of `$DSH_HOME/settings.yaml` (normally `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`). Changes are live from the next human message; no server restart is required.

Each rule has these fields:

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | empty | Human-readable label. |
| `enabled` | `true` | Whether the rule participates. |
| `mode` | `prepend` | `prepend`, `append`, `replace`, `replace-matches`, or `template`. |
| `text` | required | Injected or replacement text. It may be empty only for `replace-matches`; in `template` mode it must contain exactly one literal `{{prompt}}`. |
| `separator` | two newlines | Joiner for prepend and append; ignored by the other modes. |
| `contains` | empty | Literal substring condition; empty matches every human prompt, except `replace-matches` requires a non-empty value. |
| `caseSensitive` | `false` | Whether `contains` matching is case-sensitive. |
| `firstTurnOnly` | `false` | Apply only on turn 1 of a session. |
| `priority` | `100` | Lower numbers run first; ties use stable rule ids. |

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：Matching always examines the original human text. Text injected by an earlier rule cannot recursively trigger another rule. The plugin accepts at most 64 rules, 32,768 characters per rule, and 131,072 total rule-text characters.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：`replace-matches` changes every literal `contains` occurrence inside each text block and leaves all other text and non-text blocks in place. It is not a regular expression, so characters such as `.`, `*`, and `[` have no special meaning. `caseSensitive` controls whether letter case must match.

For example, to turn every `hello` into `你好` without changing the rest of the prompt, add this rule in the Web card:

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `hello → 你好` |
| Mode | `Replace matching text` (`replace-matches`) |
| Contains | `hello` |
| Text | `你好` |
| Case sensitive | Off to also replace `Hello` and `HELLO`; on to replace only lowercase `hello` |

With case sensitivity off, `Please say hello, HELLO!` becomes `Please say 你好, 你好!`. Set Text to an empty string to remove every match instead.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：`template` wraps the complete message content using exactly one literal `{{prompt}}` token. It is deliberately not a Handlebars-style template language: expressions, conditions, escaping, and other variables are not supported, and every character outside the single token is used verbatim. For example:

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `XML request wrapper` |
| Mode | `Template` (`template`) |
| Contains | empty to match every human prompt |
| Text | `<request>\n{{prompt}}\n</request>` |

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：For a text-only prompt, `Explain this code` becomes:

```text
<request>
Explain this code
</request>
```

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：For a multimodal prompt, the prefix and suffix stay logically outside the entire original content. A prefix is merged into the first block only when that block is text; otherwise a non-empty prefix text block is inserted before it. Likewise, a suffix is merged into the last block only when that block is text; otherwise a non-empty suffix text block is inserted after it. Images and all other non-text blocks remain in their original positions and order. `separator` is ignored in this mode. `contains`, case sensitivity, first-turn matching, priorities, and matching against the original prompt work exactly as they do for the other modes.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：Settings are shared by every session and profile using the same DSH Home. Use a different `DSH_HOME` when installations need isolated rule sets.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules in Web settings：Use one settings writer per DSH Home. Writes are serialized inside one DSH process, so its Web card and conversation tool cannot overwrite one another; two separate DSH processes writing the same `settings.yaml` section concurrently can still replace each other's rules. Give concurrently writable profiles different `DSH_HOME` values, or keep rule changes on one running process.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules from a conversation：The model receives a `prompt_rewrite_rules` tool with four actions:

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| `list` | Read rules; no approval is required. |
| `add` | Add a rule with a host-generated stable id. |
| `set_enabled` | Enable or disable a rule by id. |
| `remove` | Delete a rule by id. |

Ask naturally, for example:

```text
请添加一条 prompt rewrite 规则：
名称是“翻译 hello”，使用 replace-matches 模式，
把用户消息中每个 hello 替换成“你好”，不区分大小写。
```

Or add a template rule:

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Manage rules from a conversation：```text
请添加一条 prompt rewrite 规则：
名称是“请求标签”，使用 template 模式，
模板文本是“<request>\n{{prompt}}\n</request>”。
```

Rule mutations require a human **Allow once** approval because they persist across conversations. A newly approved rule affects only future human messages; it cannot rewrite the request that created it. `list` returns the exact ids required by `set_enabled` and `remove`.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Recovery and escape hatch：A broad `replace` rule can hide a later management request. Messages beginning with this hard-coded prefix always bypass rewriting:

```text
PROMPT_REWRITE_ADMIN: 请列出所有 prompt rewrite 规则并禁用全局 replace 规则
```

For an emergency process-wide bypass, restart DSH with:

```sh
DSH_PROMPT_REWRITE_DISABLE=1 pnpm dsh web --port 8317
```

The management tool remains available while bypassed. If necessary, stop DSH and reset the persistent section directly:

```yaml
dsh-prompt-rewrite:
  rules: {}
```

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Static per-profile rules：To keep a rule in one profile rather than shared settings, target the installed row in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`. A row patch replaces the complete plugin config:

```yaml
- id: dsh-prompt-rewrite
  config:
    rules:
      profile-example:

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Static per-profile rules：Profile rules are composition-owned. Web settings and the conversation tool may override or disable them, but cannot delete them; removing a profile rule requires editing the profile patch. The settings layer stores only fields that differ from the profile rule, so later profile edits still flow through untouched fields.

dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Migrating from the former dsh-ds4-integrated plugin：Install this bundle in each affected profile and refresh `dsh-ds4` so its obsolete prompt-rewrite row is removed. With DSH stopped, rename the old top-level settings key in `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` from `ds4-prompt-rewrite` to `dsh-prompt-rewrite`; the nested `rules` data is unchanged. Do not retain both keys.

text: dsh-prompt-rewrite README · Migrating from the former dsh-ds4-integrated plugin：The final rewritten message is the `user/message` shown in the conversation and used to reconstruct model history. The earlier inbox receipt retains the original submitted text for auditing, so this plugin is a prompt transformer, not a log-redaction mechanism.
